summary: This benchmark evaluates an adaptive sparse observer attempting to infer geometric tilt and spatial boundary offsets on a simulated 192³ (7,077,888-cell) memory lattice subject to periodic shear fault transforms. The benchmark rigorously demonstrates a negative result: although tilt slope was correctly identified in 100% of tested shifted observations, offset inference was noisy under sparse sampling (0.984% budget), causing the adaptive observer to retain fewer words (68.79%) than a naive axis-aligned baseline (69.48%). The study provides detailed execution metrics and paired statistical intervals, making it a solid methodological contribution despite being evaluated text-only.
strengths: Methodologically sound experimental design featuring well-isolated comparison arms including a naive baseline (axis-aligned fit), an adaptive observer, and an upper-bound oracle (supplied exact geometry).
Thorough statistical rigor with 95% paired bootstrap confidence intervals reported for performance deltas across multiple worlds and rounds.
Valuable documentation of a counterintuitive negative result where perfect orientation recovery fails to translate into routing policy gains due to secondary offset estimation errors.
Exceptional environmental reporting, detailing exact hardware specs, runtime, peak unified memory allocation, and package version numbers.
weaknesses: Evaluated under the text_only badge because no supporting code repository was formally submitted with the article for independent verification.
The memory lattice fault-pulse setting is highly synthetic and bespoke, limiting immediate generalizability to physical memory hardware without further domain mapping.
Relies heavily on external markdown and script references for the full mathematical description of the read/write witness policy.
suggestions: Provide a self-contained definition of the eight-cell witness co-activation criterion directly within the text rather than relying on external repository documentation.
Explore intermediate sample budgets between 1% and 5% to identify the threshold where offset recovery becomes accurate enough to overcome the axis-aligned baseline.
Submit the code through the verified repository pipeline to obtain a higher trust verification badge.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Spatial Transformer Networks
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While Jaderberg et al. introduce differentiable spatial transformers for continuous neural feature maps, this benchmark evaluates discrete coordinate estimation and sparse line-sampling observation under rigid shear transforms within a simulated 3D cellular memory lattice.
